primitives.name: Discriminant Analysis
primitives.verbatim_quote: A 2x3 (game location: home and away; playing position: guards, forwards and centres) factorial MANOVA followed by a discriminant analysis was performed.
primitives.assumptions: Multivariate normality of game-related statistics within groups, homogeneity of covariance matrices, linear relationships between variables, absence of multicollinearity among predictors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity when the number of observations is less than the number of variables or perfect separation occurs.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Maps to posterior predictive distributions via quadratic discriminant functions. GSE - Models state transitions between home vs away performance manifolds.
layer2.telemetry: Model accuracy on holdout validation sets, eigenvalue ratios of covariance matrices, misclassification rates

primitives.name: Assertive Performance
primitives.verbatim_quote: Results suggested a differential effect of home advantage in basketball players by role in the team, with guards from home teams playing more assertively, whereas in away teams forwards played more assertively.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that assertiveness can be operationally defined by the game-related statistics used (FGM2, FTM2, REBdef, AST, STL, BLK, PF).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails when statistical power is insufficient to detect position-specific effects, or when confounding factors (team quality, match importance) are uncontrolled.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Encodes prior beliefs about assertion levels using Dirichlet process mixtures. GSE - Transitions between high/low assertion states based on location and position.
layer2.telemetry: Observed frequency of high-assertion plays (e.g., steals, blocks) relative to baseline, change in assist-to-turnover ratio

primitives.name: Territorial Drive
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theoretical explanations for this phenomenon are many and varied, including biological-based theories of territoriality, social psychology drive theories, social cognitive theories and sociological theories of community celebration (for a review see Courneya and Carron, 1992).
primitives.assumptions: Operationalizes territorial behavior as increased physical engagement (rebounds, blocks, steals) and aggressive fouling, driven by social psychological mechanisms.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Collapses when external factors (referee bias, crowd noise) overwhelm internal motivational drives.

layer2.mapping: GSI - Maps to conformal prediction regions for territorial metrics (rebounds, blocks) under home advantage null. GSE - Uses Markov decision processes to model escalation of territorial actions.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in rebound margins, block frequency, foul calls favoring home team

The three primitives form a coherent mathematical triptych: Discriminant Analysis provides the empirical classification of performance manifolds, Assertive Performance quantifies the behavioral shift along those manifolds, and Territorial Drive offers the theoretical foundation for why such shifts occur. Their dual failure mode is multicollinearity among statistics (e.g., high correlation between assists and steals), which collapses discriminant dimensions and introduces spurious assertion measures. Cross-layer veto conditions require ensuring that telemetry metrics are independent across layers: e.g., referee bias affecting territorial drive should not directly inflate assist counts, necessitating residualization in the discriminant model.
